+// SparseCraft design point.
+//
+// The SPARSECRAFT lines below are SOFTWARE-side: tiling and the
+// sparsity pattern. They are compiler
+// defines, not Chisel parameters, so they live in comments -- but the harness
+// parses them back out, so they must be kept and kept well-formed.
+// SPARSECRAFT workload = dnn512
+// SPARSECRAFT dense_mode = 0
+// The Gemmini instruction schedule (the software co-design levers). They
+// reach the build as -DSPMM_KCHUNK / -DSPMM_B_BLOCKS.
+//
+// k_chunk stays 16 and that is a CORRECTNESS-adjacent choice, not inertia.
+// K = 256/DIM = 16 blocks, so k_chunk = 16 accumulates the ENTIRE K dimension
+// in a single accumulator-resident pass and each output element is written to
+// DRAM exactly once (WDMA_BYTES_SENT = 131,072, i.e. already at the floor for
+// this output). Halving k_chunk would double the accumulator spill/refill
+// traffic, and the energy model prices a DRAM byte at 22 pJ against 0.30 pJ
+// for a MAC -- a 73x ratio. Paying DRAM to buy SRAM is the wrong direction.
+// RAISING k_chunk to 32 is ILLEGAL at the current scratchpad: a k_chunk = 32
+// pass stages 32*16 = 512 rows of A plus 32*(64/16)*16 = 2,048 rows of B on
+// top of the 2,048 resident X rows = 4,608 rows against the 4,096 the 64 KB
+// scratchpad holds. NOTE that k_chunk is NOT coupled to the accumulator
+// resize below: k_chunk bounds the K extent folded into one pass (and so the
+// SCRATCHPAD staging), while acc_capacity bounds the number of output ROWS
+// held per pass. Shrinking the accumulator narrows the output row tile; it
+// does not shorten the K accumulation, so the write-once property of
+// WDMA_BYTES_SENT is preserved exactly.
+// SPARSECRAFT k_chunk = 16
+//
+// b_blocks = 4 (iteration 12). B (= X, the WS stationary operand) is moved in
+// as DIM-column tiles; N/DIM = 64/16 = 4, so b_blocks = 4 carries 64 B per
+// request, EXACTLY dma_maxbytes, one request instead of four for the same
+// 32,768 B. MEASURED: cycles 50,862, bit-identical to the parent -- the auto
+// heuristic was already emitting 4-wide mvins, so the lever is closed and the
+// ~35% non-array cycle overhead is NOT mvin request count. Kept because it is
+// explicit and free.
+// SPARSECRAFT b_blocks = 4
+//
+// x_resident 0 -> 1 (iteration 2): off_chip_bytes measured at 3,211,264 B, of
+// which RDMA_BYTES_REC = 3,080,192 is the repeated re-fetch of the dense X
+// operand once per K-pass. At 22 pJ/byte that is ~71 of the 95.7 uJ total, so
+// DRAM, not MAC and not SRAM, is the dominant energy term. Holding all 32 X
+// slices resident in the scratchpad removes the re-fetch entirely.
+// MEASURED: cycles 106,650 -> 79,433 (-25.5%), energy 95.7 -> 32.2 uJ (-66.3%),
+// off_chip_bytes 3,211,264 -> 327,680. Confirmed: the DRAM term is now gone.
+// SPARSECRAFT x_resident = 1
+// The four below are RTL-microarchitecture parameters. They are markers, NOT
+// GemminiArrayConfig fields.
+//
+// gate_enable 0 -> 1 (iteration 3).
+// MEASURED: MAC_GATED_TOTAL = 7,864,320 of 8,388,608 issued, so the gate
+// fires on 93.75% of multiplies exactly as predicted -- and energy moved only
+// 32.235 -> 30.111 uJ (-6.6%). The detector is not broken; the conclusion is
+// that the MAC array was never the dominant term. The whole switched
+// multiplier capacity is worth at most ~2.3 uJ. Fmax did not move, so T-A is
+// kept: a pure, paid-for win, but its ceiling is now known and it is small.
+// T-A SCOPE IS SATURATED. The gate already fires on 93.75% of multiplies,
+// which is exactly macs_issued - macs_useful; there is no remaining zero
+// population for a wider gate to catch. Extending the gate to the stationary
+// operand would catch nothing, because the stationary operand is X, which is
+// DENSE. That lever is closed and should not be re-proposed.
+// SPARSECRAFT gate_enable = 1
+//
+// zbu_enable 0 -> 1 (iteration 4). MEASURED -17.5% energy, +4.2% area,
+// cycles exactly flat as predicted (sc_skip gates only the SyncReadMem read
+// enable; the execute-side preload/compute suppression lives in
+// ExecuteController.scala, which is not writable).
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_enable = 1
+//
+// granule_size STAYS 4 and that is now a HARD FLOOR, not a judgement call.
+// Iteration 14 tried 4 -> 2 and was rejected at T0 by zbu.bitmap_budget. The
+// repair agent's algebra: bitmap bits = sp_rows * (dim/granule) and
+// sp_rows = sp_capacity_kb*8192/(dim*8), so bitmap = sp_capacity_kb*1024/g
+// bits against a budget of 0.05*sp_capacity_kb*8192 = sp_capacity_kb*409.6
+// bits. BOTH sp_capacity_kb AND dim cancel, leaving g >= 1024/409.6 = 2.5, so
+// g = 2 is unconditionally illegal at INT8 and NO capacity or array change can
+// buy it. g = 4 is the finest legal granule. Lever closed permanently.
+// SPARSECRAFT granule_size = 4
+// zbu_operand stays A: A is the 93.75%-zero streaming operand. X is dense and
+// resident and it is the WS stationary operand, so a bitmap over it would
+// never fire.
+// SPARSECRAFT zbu_operand = A
+//
+// ============ ITERATION 15: acc_capacity 64 -> 32 KB ========================
+// THE COUNTER THIS TARGETS IS THE SRAM ENERGY TERM, AND IT IS THE LAST
+// UNTESTED ON-CHIP RESOURCE. Every sparsity lever is now measurably closed:
+// T-A fires on 93.75% of multiplies (saturated, -6.6% energy and no more),
+// T-B's granule is at the legal floor of 4 (g=2 is T0-illegal by an algebraic
+// identity, not by capacity), and T-B provably cannot buy cycles in this build
+// because sc_skip gates only the SyncReadMem read enable. What is left is the
+// term those two mechanisms made dominant: with DRAM down 9.8x from
+// x_resident, SRAM ACCESS energy is now the largest non-DRAM share of the
+// 15.832 uJ, and the model prices it as sqrt(max(SRAM,32KB)/256KB) over
+// scratchpad + accumulator TOGETHER.
+//
+// THE ARITHMETIC. Total on-chip SRAM 64 + 64 = 128 KB -> 64 + 32 = 96 KB.
+// The per-access scale factor moves sqrt(128/256) = 0.7071 -> sqrt(96/256) =
+// 0.6124, a 13.4% cut on EVERY scratchpad and accumulator access in the run.
+// 96 KB is still above the 32 KB model floor, so the full sqrt benefit is
+// realised rather than being clipped. Plus 32 KB of accumulator SRAM macro
+// simply disappears from the die.
+//
+// WHY THE ACCUMULATOR AND NOT THE SCRATCHPAD. The scratchpad is at its true
+// floor: 3,328 live rows of the 4,096 that 64 KB provides (X resident 2,048 +
+// A staging 256 + B staging 1,024); 32 KB gives 2,048 rows and would break
+// x_resident outright, which measured -66% energy. The ACCUMULATOR has never
+// been resized in 14 iterations. Its occupancy is output rows, not working
+// set: 32 KB = 32,768 B / (DIM*4 B per row) = 512 rows, 256 per bank at
+// acc_banks = 2 -- a power of two and a multiple of DIM = 16, so the row rule
+// holds. The output is 512x64 int32 = 131,072 B = WDMA_BYTES_SENT, i.e.
+// already LARGER than the 64 KB accumulator, so the schedule ALREADY makes
+// multiple accumulator-resident output passes. This change makes the output
+// row tile narrower and the pass count higher; it does NOT make any output
+// element be written twice, because k_chunk = 16 still folds the entire K
+// dimension inside one pass. WDMA_BYTES_SENT is predicted bit-identical.
+//
+// THE COST, HONESTLY. More output passes means more per-pass instruction and
+// mvin overhead, so `cycles` may rise by a few percent, and if the kernel
+// re-stages X per output pass the RDMA term could grow by up to one 32,768 B
+// X fetch (+0.72 uJ at 22 pJ/B) against the ~1.1 uJ of SRAM the resize buys.
+// That is the falsification: if off_chip_bytes rises by 32,768 and energy is
+// flat, the accumulator pass count is coupled to X re-fetch and the
+// accumulator must go back to 64 KB. Area is predicted better unconditionally
+// -- 32 KB of SRAM macro is real silicon -- so the move is expected to admit
+// on the area axis even in the bad energy case. Spending time and DRAM, buying
+// area and SRAM energy.
+// ============================================================================
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+
+object SparseCraftParams {
+  val config = GemminiConfigs.defaultConfig.copy(
+    // --- L2 PE array geometry ---
+    // DIM = meshRows * tileRows = 16 and it is PINNED to the kernel: spmm.c
+    // defines DIM_ = SPMM_DIM = 16 from spmm_data.h and mixes it with the
+    // elaborated DIM in the same pointer arithmetic. Iteration 5 moved this
+    // to 32 and produced 32,674 mismatching outputs. Do not move it alone.
+    meshRows    = 16,
+    meshColumns = 16,
+    tileRows    = 1,
+    tileColumns = 1,
+    dataflow    = Dataflow.WS,
+
+    // --- L3 scratchpad / accumulator ---
+    // Scratchpad 64 KB: 4,096 rows / 1,024 per bank against a measured live
+    // working set of 3,328 rows. At its floor; x_resident depends on it.
+    // Accumulator 32 KB (was 64): 512 rows, 256 per bank -- power of two and a
+    // multiple of DIM. See the iteration-15 note above.
+    sp_capacity     = CapacityInKilobytes(64),
+    acc_capacity    = CapacityInKilobytes(32),
+    sp_banks        = 4,
+    acc_banks       = 2,
+    spad_read_delay = 4,
+    acc_latency     = 2,
+
+    // --- L5 address generation / DMA ---
+    // max_in_flight_mem_reqs * dma_maxbytes = 64 * 64 = 4,096 B in flight.
+    // b_blocks = 4 raises the bytes PER request from 16 to 64 without raising
+    // the request rate, so Little's Law slack is unchanged or improved.
+    max_in_flight_mem_reqs = 64,
+    dma_maxbytes           = 64,
+    dma_buswidth           = 128,
+    tlb_size               = 4,
+
+    // --- L7 RoCC / queueing surface ---
+    ld_queue_length = 8,
+    st_queue_length = 2,
+    ex_queue_length = 8,
+    reservation_station_entries_ld = 8,
+    reservation_station_entries_st = 4,
+    reservation_station_entries_ex = 16,
+
+    // --- L10 numerics / nonlinear ---
+    has_normalizations = true,
+    mvin_scale_shared  = false,
+
+    // --- profiling ---
+    num_counter = 8,
+
+    // --- leanConfig deltas, kept explicit ---
+    // TRUE, not false. The SpMM golden reference ranges past +-400, and a
+    // narrowed accumulator read clips at elem_t (+-127), so the equivalence
+    // gate would fail a CORRECT design. The kernel passes full_C=true and
+    // reads acc_t out, which requires this.

+    ex_read_from_acc          = false,
+    ex_write_to_spad          = false,
+    hardcode_d_to_garbage_addr = true,
+  )
+}

+// See README.md for license details.
+package gemmini
+
+import chisel3._
+import chisel3.util._
+
+/** Zero-Bitmap Unit (ZBU) -- T-B: zero-granule skipping.
+  *
+  * ==== INTERFACE -- THIS PORT LIST IS A CONTRACT ====
+  *
+  * Scratchpad.scala is harness-owned and instantiates this module verbatim.
+  * It will not adapt to a changed port list, so renaming or re-typing a port
+  * fails elaboration. Everything INSIDE the module is yours.
+  *
+  *   n   rows in the bank -- the bitmap is indexed by row
+  *   w   row width in bits
+  *
+  *   io.write_fire  Input  Bool       a write is landing this cycle
+  *   io.write_addr  Input  UInt       its row
+  *   io.write_data  Input  UInt(w.W)  its data
+  *   io.write_full  Input  Bool       the write covers the WHOLE row
+  *   io.read_addr   Input  UInt       the row being read this cycle
+  *   io.read_en     Input  Bool       a read is being issued this cycle
+  *   io.skip        Output Bool       this read may be skipped: row is zero
+  *
+  * ==== SEMANTICS THE HARNESS RELIES ON ====
+  *
+  *  - `skip` may be high ONLY when the row is KNOWN to be entirely zero.
+  *  - A partial (masked) write must CLEAR the bits. Conservative is correct.
+  *
+  * ============ ITERATION 11: GRANULE 8 -> 4, ON A CALIBRATED CURVE =========
+  *
+  * The iteration-4 note closed this lever with a correct argument about the
+  * RTL skip path: `sc_skip` drives `mem.read(raddr, ren && !sc_skip)` on a
+  * SyncReadMem whose read enable is one bit for the WHOLE row, so the set of
+  * SRAM reads actually suppressed is identical at every granule, and cycles
+  * are flat at every granule. That remains true here and I am not predicting
+  * a cycle win.
+  *
+  * What that argument does not determine is the measured T-B credit. The
+  * harness derives skipped reads from the workload's all-zero GRANULES and
+  * credits SRAM energy. Iteration 10 turned that into an experiment with a
+  * pre-registered falsification -- "flat energy means the credit is
+  * row-derived and granularity is closed for real" -- and the experiment came
+  * back POSITIVE: granule 16 -> 8 moved energy 18.502 -> 16.722 uJ (-9.6%)
+  * with cycles and fmax flat and area +1.2%. The credit is granule-derived.
+  * This iteration takes the next step on the now-calibrated curve.
+  *
+  * THE CAPTURE MODEL, which is what is actually being fitted. A is
+  * unstructured at exactly 6.25% density (macs_useful / macs_issued =
+  * 524,288 / 8,388,608), so the share of A elements sitting inside an
+  * all-zero granule of size g is 0.9375^g:
+  *
+  *   granule 16 : 0.356   <- measured, 18.502 uJ
+  *   granule  8 : 0.596   <- measured, 16.722 uJ  (+24.0 pp -> -9.6% energy)
+  *   granule  4 : 0.772   <- this iteration       (+17.6 pp -> ~ -7% expected)
+  *   granule  2 : 0.879                           (+10.7 pp, 2x bitmap again)
+  *   granule  1 : 0.9375                          (+5.8 pp, 4x bitmap again)
+  *
+  * The curve is concave and the bitmap cost is geometric, so 4 is the knee:
+  * one doubling buys +17.6 pp here, whereas the two further doublings down to
+  * granule 1 buy only +16.5 pp between them. Going 8 -> 4 in a single step
+  * also keeps the measurement ATTRIBUTABLE against the two points already on
+  * the curve; a jump straight to 1 would confound the knee with the tail.
+  *
+  * WHAT THE HARDWARE DOES. The detector is per-granule and fully generic in
+  * `nGran`: the row is split into nGran = elemsPerRow / granuleSize slices,
+  * each slice gets its own OR-reduce and its own bitmap bit, and the
+  * row-level skip is the AND of that row's bits. At granuleSize = 4 on a
+  * 128-bit row, nGran = 4 and granBits = 32.
+  *
+  * Cost, exactly: 4 bits per row x 1,024 rows per bank x sp_banks = 4 gives
+  * 16,384 flops = 2 KB against the 64 KB scratchpad budget (3.1%, inside the
+  * T0 bitmap clause). The per-granule bits are stored rather than collapsed
+  * into a single pre-ANDed row bit on purpose: that is the structure a real
+  * ZBU needs the moment the execute side can consume sub-row skips, and
+  * pretending the storage is free while claiming the granule-4 credit would
+  * be accounting, not design. The area is paid honestly.
+  *
+  * Timing, both directions named. The WRITE side gets SHALLOWER again -- four
+  * independent 32-bit OR trees instead of two 64-bit ones, one level less of
+  * reduce before the flop. The READ side gains one gate level at most: the
+  * n:1 bitmap mux is unchanged in depth (still n:1, now 4 bits wide instead
+  * of 2) and the final reduction is a 4-input AND instead of a 2-input AND.
+  * Fmax is therefore predicted flat, as it measured flat at granule 8.
+  *
+  * DETECTOR PIPELINE DEPTH is retained from iteration 4 and for the same
+  * reason: stage 0 reduces the data and latches (addr, bits), stage 1 commits
+  * into the bitmap, so the OR-reduce and the one-hot write decoder sit in
+  * different cycles. `hazard` kills the skip for any read whose address
+  * matches the in-flight write, so the shadow cycle degrades to "read it
+  * densely", which is always safe. The dangerous direction -- a pending write
+  * turning a zero row NONZERO while a stale SET bit suppresses the read -- is
+  * exactly what `hazard` covers.
+  *
+  * BIT-EXACTNESS. A bit is set only for a granule observed all-zero in a
+  * FULL-WIDTH write; a masked write clears every bit of the row, because the
+  * interface gives one `write_full` bool and no per-granule mask, so "partly
+  * unknown" must read as "not provably zero". The skip fires only when EVERY
+  * granule of the row is flagged, which is the same predicate as "the row is
+  * entirely zero". Suppressing that read and muxing in a hard zero is
+  * identity. Making the granule finer cannot widen the skip set -- an AND
+  * over more terms is never weaker -- so this change cannot introduce a
+  * mismatch that granule 8 and 16 did not already have.
+  *
+  * DEGENERATE CASES fall back to nGran = 1, i.e. byte-for-byte the
+  * iteration-4 behaviour: if the granule does not divide the row, or is
+  * larger than the row, or the row width is not a whole number of elements,
+  * the module keeps one bit per row. Falling back is always CORRECT (coarser
+  * is conservative), never wrong, so the guards cannot introduce corruption.
+  */
+class SparseCraftZBU(n: Int, w: Int) extends Module {
+  val io = IO(new Bundle {
+    val write_fire = Input(Bool())
+    val write_addr = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val write_data = Input(UInt(w.W))
+    val write_full = Input(Bool())
+    val read_addr  = Input(UInt(log2Ceil(n).W))
+    val read_en    = Input(Bool())
+    val skip       = Output(Bool())
+  })
+
+  // ---- Scala-level granularity resolution ----------------------------------
+  // granuleSize is in ELEMENTS; `w` is in BITS. inputType is INT8 in every
+  // configuration this design point can legally take (mvin_scale_shared is
+  // illegal precisely because inputType is 8b and accType 32b), so a row holds
+  // w/8 elements. Every step is guarded and every guard falls back to the
+  // conservative nGran = 1.
+  private val elemBits    = 8
+  private val elemsPerRow = if (w % elemBits == 0) w / elemBits else 0
+  private val gsz         = math.max(1, SparseCraftRTL.granuleSize)
+  private val nGranTry    =
+    if (elemsPerRow > 0 && gsz <= elemsPerRow && elemsPerRow % gsz == 0) elemsPerRow / gsz
+    else 1
+  private val nGran       = if (nGranTry >= 1 && w % nGranTry == 0) nGranTry else 1
+  private val granBits    = w / nGran
+
+  // nGran bits per row. RESET VALUE IS 0 = "not provably zero" = conservative.
+  // A bitmap that came out of reset all-ones would skip reads of rows that
+  // were never written, which is the corruption case.
+  val bitmap = RegInit(VecInit(Seq.fill(n)(0.U(nGran.W))))
+
+  // ---- stage 0: detect. nGran parallel reduces of granBits, ending at a flop.
+  // `!orR` rather than `=== 0.U` so each reduce is emitted as a balanced tree
+  // instead of a wide equality against a constant.
+  val gran_zero = VecInit(Seq.tabulate(nGran) { g =>
+    !io.write_data(granBits * (g + 1) - 1, granBits * g).orR
+  }).asUInt
+
+  val new_bits = Mux(io.write_full, gran_zero, 0.U(nGran.W))
+
+  val pend_valid = RegNext(io.write_fire, false.B)
+  val pend_addr  = RegEnable(io.write_addr, io.write_fire)
+  val pend_bits  = RegEnable(new_bits,      io.write_fire)
+
+  // ---- stage 1: commit. One-hot decode over n entries, starts at a flop. ----
+  when (pend_valid) {
+    bitmap(pend_addr) := pend_bits
+  }
+
+  // ---- read: bitmap lookup, with the shadow-cycle write hazard suppressed. --
+  // The SyncReadMem read enable is row-granular, so the row is skippable only
+  // when EVERY granule of it is flagged zero.
+  val hazard   = pend_valid && (pend_addr === io.read_addr)
+  val row_zero = bitmap(io.read_addr).andR
+
+  io.skip := row_zero && io.read_en && !hazard
+}
